[LNUL.5.2] **Guard narrowing.** Inside `x is not null and <…>`, flow typing makes
`x` a `T` (non-null) in the right operand. Same for the `where`-clause tail
after an `is not null` conjunct. The narrowing is scoped to the `where`-clause (the
remaining conjuncts); it does **not** flow across the LHS→RHS boundary into the
action body. An action referencing a binding guarded on the LHS still sees it as
`T?` and must handle absence at each concrete-value position with `??` — there is
no LHS→RHS data-flow analysis ([LNUL.5.4]). So `Sensor s where s.state is not null ->
emit Out(value = s.state)` is a compile error (`value` is a non-nullable slot);
the author writes `value = s.state ?? 0.0`.

**Narrowing is a typing rule, not an evaluation order.** It decides which
positions type-check; the conjuncts may still be evaluated in any order
([LNUL.4.2]). A narrowed conjunct evaluated before its guard meets the `null`
the guard excludes, and may raise; the guard is then `false` and absorbs what it
raised, so the conjunction answers as though the guard had run first.

The guard is spelled `is not null` and not `!= null`: the latter is a compile
error ([LNUL.4.4]), and it could not have narrowed anything anyway, because a
propagating comparison never establishes that the operand is present.
